claim_boundary: Maps each PUBLISHED ARTIFACT to the mechanisms that guard it and records when each mechanism last ran, by running it. It does not claim any guard is correct — only which claims have one and which do not. Runs no backtest, opens no return data, registers no hypothesis identity. 0 trials.

tail: ALL CHECKS REPRODUCED. The published numbers match their hashes/signatures, and the engine is byte-deterministic.
PASS — no withdrawn claim is asserted anywhere in the publish set
every numeral a reader can see traces to a published artifact
README audit passed: 108 papers, 13 topic hubs, 84 measurements, 234 URLs, 228 packets (226 incomplete); deploy-gate source verified

mechanisms.CONTENT_HASH: recomputed by the published reproduce kit; proves it was not edited after publication and nothing about whether it is right
mechanisms.HOST_MIRROR: both hosts receive the identical file — the weakest, because it says two copies agree and nothing about what they say
mechanisms.NAMED_GUARD: a test or verifier that mentions this artifact specifically
mechanisms.RENDERED_PAGE: rendered as a measurement page and checked for a claim boundary

what_mirror_only_means: We verify both hosts received the identical file, and nothing verifies the file. No test names it, it carries no content hash, it renders on no page. If its contents went stale or wrong, both hosts would publish the same wrong thing and every check would pass.
why: Split coverage reads as coverage. Every guard here reports on itself and none reported on the set, so an artifact with no guard looked exactly like one with three.
why_rebuild_first: The publish path rebuilds the derived contracts before anything checks them, so a suite observed before that rebuild reports a failure the publish never ships. The first run of this map did exactly that.
